newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's publishes capital security plans next week.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's publishes capital security plans next week.

text.p: Lloyd's of London said on Friday it will lay out next week its final proposals to strengthen the financial security framework which underpins it.
Last month the insurance market published the plans of a working party designed to strengthen Lloyd's 'chain of security'.
The effect of the proposals would be to increase the amount of capital that Names - the traditional backers of Lloyd's - would have to put up to back their underwriting activity.
A period of consultation came to an end on May 16.

Speaking at the insurance market's global results presentation, Lloyd's chairman Sir David Rowland said they had received "some interesting reactions" and all contributions had been taken into account.
But he said the focus was on having fairness among capital providers in the market.
Chief executive Ron Sandler added that the principle of 'user pays' - that different forms of capital "pays its own way" also applied.
Corporate members were introduced to Lloyd's for the first time in 1994 but now account for 44 percent of total market capacity.
Names fear they are effectively being driven out in favour of corporate capital, a charge repeatedly denied by the Lloyd's hierarchy.

Names groups are reported to have called for an extension of the proposed transition period for the tougher capital requirements of four or five years rather than three years though they have welcomed the general thrust of the review.
